claims.text: In C# 14, class X : Y declares X as derived from base class Y; a variable declared with a base class type can hold an object of any class derived from it, so the object's run-time type (the class named after new) can differ from the variable's declared type.

claims.text: An abstract method is declared with abstract and no body and is permitted only in an abstract class; a non-abstract class must have an implementation of every inherited abstract method, so a non-abstract class that derives directly from the abstract class must supply it with an override method.
claims.source_hint: csharp/language-reference/keywords/abstract.md l.47, l.54 ('only permitted in abstract classes'), l.55, l.61 ('provided by a method override')

claims.text: When code calls a virtual method through a base-type variable, .NET looks up the object's run-time type when the call runs and invokes that type's override; an abstract method is implicitly virtual.
claims.source_hint: fundamentals/object-oriented/polymorphism.md ('the CLR looks up the run-time type of the object, and invokes that override'); keywords/abstract.md ('implicitly a virtual method')
